title: routing: strict mode — fail loudly when no rule matches an unrecognized model
description:
## Problem

When agent.routing.rules is configured but no rule matches the active model, NEEDLE silently falls back to agent.default (or routing.default_adapter if set). This means a misconfigured or unrecognized model (e.g. a new provider, a typo, a model removed from the adapter list) routes silently to the wrong adapter with no signal to the operator.

## What to add

Add an optional boolean agent.routing.strict (default: false):

  agent:
    routing:
      strict: true
      rules:
        - match_model: "(claude-)?(sonnet|opus|fable|haiku).*"
          adapter: claude-print
        - match_model: "glm.*"
          adapter: claude-code-glm-4.7

When strict: true and no rule matches the active model:
1. Do NOT fall back to agent.default or routing.default_adapter.
2. Emit a RoutingFailed telemetry event with the model name and rule count.
3. Return Err from apply_routing_rules with a clear human-readable message:
   "no routing rule matched model 'gpt-4o' — add a rule to agent.routing.rules or set routing.strict: false to fall back to the default adapter"
4. Propagates through resolve_adapter -> dispatch -> marks the bead as failed (not orphaned), surfaced in the bead list.

## Schema changes

pub struct RoutingConfig {
    pub rules: Vec<RoutingRule>,
    pub default_adapter: Option<String>,
    pub strict: bool,  // new, default false
}

Add RoutingFailed to EventKind:
RoutingFailed {
    bead_id: BeadId,
    model: String,
    rules_tried: usize,
}

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] RoutingConfig has strict: bool (default false); existing configs without strict behave unchanged.
- [ ] strict: true + no match: apply_routing_rules returns Err with the message above; RoutingFailed telemetry emitted.
- [ ] strict: false + no match: existing fallback behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Bead is marked failed (dispatch error), not orphaned or silently retried.
- [ ] Unit tests: strict=true no-match -> Err; strict=false no-match -> default; strict=true match -> Ok.
- [ ] cargo test passes (push and wait for needle-ci).

Root cause identified and documented in notes/bf-2bw-triage.md

title: Worker startup: validate configured adapter exists before accepting work
description:
Even after bf-14w removes the silent fallback in resolve_adapter, a worker with a misconfigured adapter will fail only at dispatch time (after claiming a bead). It should fail at startup, before claiming any beads.

## What to add

In the worker initialization path (before the main loop begins), call resolve_adapter() once as a preflight check:

  // In Worker::new() or the run() entry point, before the claim loop:
  self.resolve_adapter().context("startup adapter preflight failed")?;

If this returns Err, the worker should exit immediately with a clear error message printed to stderr:
  'NEEDLE: agent adapter "claude-code-glm-47" not found — aborting. Check ~/.needle/agents/ or the agents config directory.'

This prevents a worker from running for hours, repeatedly claiming and failing beads, when the adapter was never configured correctly.

## Complete when
- Starting needle with --agent nonexistent-adapter exits immediately with a clear error (not after the first bead claim)
- The error message names the missing adapter and suggests where to look
- cargo test passes (push to main and wait for needle-ci)

title: Model-based adapter routing: Anthropic subscription models -> claude-print, default claude-code-glm-4.7 (June 15 deadline)
description:
## Context (recreated 2026-06-11 — original bead chain bf-22v/bf-6hp/bf-2pp was lost in a workspace rebuild)

DEADLINE: June 15, 2026 — Anthropic Agent SDK credit split. After that date, plain `claude -p` dispatches bill API credits instead of subscription.

Policy (user-set): claude-print is the default adapter ONLY for Anthropic claude models on subscription billing — sonnet, opus, fable, haiku. ALL other models default to the existing `claude-code-glm-4.7` adapter.

## Current state
Adapter selection is adapter-name-static per worker (Worker::resolve_adapter, src/worker/mod.rs ~line 2812): config.agent.default -> workspace .needle.yaml -> env -> CLI. The model is a field ON the adapter; model never influences adapter choice. The claude-print adapter yaml is already installed at ~/.config/needle/adapters/claude-print.yaml and the binary works (~/.local/bin/claude-print).

## Implement
1. Config schema: `agent.routing` — ordered list of {model_pattern (regex/glob), adapter} rules, first-match-wins, workspace-overridable via .needle.yaml; `default_adapter: claude-code-glm-4.7` fallback.
2. Ship default rules: pattern matching anthropic claude sonnet/opus/fable/haiku model names -> claude-print.
3. Apply routing in resolve_adapter/dispatch when a model is requested; emit a routing-decision telemetry event (model, matched rule, chosen adapter).
4. NO silent fallback: if the routed adapter is missing, fail the dispatch loudly (complements bf-14w and bf-2wi — do not duplicate their scope).
5. Update docs/plan.md with the routing policy + June 15 rationale.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unit tests: pattern matching, first-match-wins, workspace override, default fallback.
- [ ] Requesting a sonnet/opus/fable/haiku model routes to claude-print; glm-4.7 routes to claude-code-glm-4.7.
- [ ] Missing routed adapter = loud dispatch failure (no builtin claude-sonnet fallback).
- [ ] cargo build + tests green.

title: Add real concurrent claim exclusivity property test using actual flock
description:
The plan (Test Strategy, Property Tests) specifies: 'Claim Exclusivity: Given N concurrent claim attempts on 1 bead, exactly 1 succeeds.'

The current test in `tests/property_tests.rs` (Property 3) explicitly acknowledges it only tests the structural exclusion set property — not actual concurrent locking. The comment reads: 'We can't easily test concurrent claiming without a real bead store, but we CAN verify the structural property.'

This is a gap. The plan requires a test that actually exercises the flock-based serialization with N goroutine-equivalent workers racing to claim the same bead.

## Deliverables
- Add a new property test (or integration test in `tests/real_br_integration_tests.rs`) that:
  1. Creates a single bead in a real `br` workspace
  2. Spawns N Tokio tasks, each running through the `Claimer::claim_next()` path
  3. Asserts exactly 1 task receives `ClaimOutcome::Claimed`, the rest receive `ClaimOutcome::AllRaceLost` or `ClaimOutcome::NoCandidates`
- Property should be parameterized over N (2..=20 workers)
- Must use real flock via `fs2` (no mocking)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test passes consistently under `cargo test --features integration` with real `br` binary
- [ ] N=2, N=5, N=20 all assert exactly 1 success
- [ ] Test is documented with 'Property 3 (true concurrent)' comment

title: Document Splice strand and commit-trailer injection in plan.md
description:
Two significant features exist in code that are absent from `docs/plan/plan.md`:

1. **Splice strand** (`src/strand/splice.rs`, ~1074 LOC) — a strand that documents worker failures. Not described anywhere in the plan's Strand Waterfall section, which defines strands 1-7 (Pluck, Mend, Explore, Weave, Unravel, Pulse, Knot) + Reflect (Phase 4). Splice is numbered and sequenced but not in the plan.

2. **Commit-trailer injection** (`src/commit_hook.rs`, ~164 LOC) — NEEDLE amends the latest commit to add a `Bead-Id: <id>` trailer after successful bead close, for HOOP bead_commit_index integration. This feature is not mentioned anywhere in the plan.

Both features are implemented, tested, and in production. The plan is the authoritative specification — it should be updated to document these features so future workers understand why they exist.

## Deliverables
- Add a **Strand 8: Splice** section to the Strand Waterfall chapter in `docs/plan/plan.md`
  - Purpose, entry conditions, algorithm, exit conditions, guardrails
  - Its position in the waterfall (where it fits relative to Knot/Reflect)
- Add a **Commit Trailer Injection** section to the Architecture chapter or Agent Adapters chapter
  - Describe the `Bead-Id:` trailer format
  - Describe when it fires (success + commits detected)
  - Describe the HOOP integration context
- Update the module boundary table to include `commit_hook` and `strand/splice`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Plan accurately describes Splice strand algorithm and position in waterfall
- [ ] Plan accurately describes commit-trailer injection trigger and format
- [ ] No code features are undocumented in the plan

title: Emit structured fleet.cpu_saturated and fleet.memory_low telemetry events
description:
The plan specifies (Concurrency section, Fleet Sizing) that NEEDLE emits a `fleet.cpu_saturated` event when system load exceeds `cpu_load_warn` threshold, and implies a corresponding memory warning event.

Currently `check_system_resources()` in `src/rate_limit/mod.rs` uses `tracing::warn!` log macros rather than structured telemetry events. This violates design principle 4 (Observable by default: every state transition emits structured telemetry) and the plan's event catalog is incomplete without these events.

## Deliverables
- Add `FleetCpuSaturated { load_average: f64, threshold: f64, core_count: usize }` variant to `EventKind` in `src/telemetry/mod.rs`
- Add `FleetMemoryLow { free_mb: u64, threshold_mb: u64 }` variant to `EventKind`
- Update `check_system_resources()` in `src/rate_limit/mod.rs` to accept a `&Telemetry` sink and emit these events instead of (or in addition to) the tracing log
- Update call sites in `src/worker/mod.rs` to pass the telemetry sink
- Add the two event types to the telemetry documentation in `docs/plan/plan.md` (Health event catalog)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `fleet.cpu_saturated` event appears in JSONL log when load exceeds threshold
- [ ] `fleet.memory_low` event appears in JSONL log when free RAM drops below threshold
- [ ] Both events carry the numeric values (actual vs threshold) in their `data` field
- [ ] Events are exported via OTLP sink (severity WARN)
